title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR stands in for Charles Martel — a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours, and a completely different polity
SALADIN stands in for Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi — an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of the 1180s from Egypt/Syria, not an 8th-century Umayyad governor of al-Andalus
EL_CID stands in for Duke Odo of Aquitaine — a Castilian magnate of the 1090s, wrong century and wrong realm
CROSSBOWMAN x2 in the Frankish roster: the crossbow was not a battlefield arm of Carolingian Francia in 732
PIKEMAN x4 for the Frankish shield wall: the massed pike is a 14th-century development; SPEARMAN/MILITIA-line would have been the period-appropriate engine choice
KNIGHT x9 as the core of the Umayyad army — the fully-armoured Frankish-style knight is a poor stand-in when the engine offers LIGHT_CAVALRY/CAMEL_RIDER and Saracen-style raiders

MONASTERY in the Frankish camp is a generic Western European chapel building rather than anything tied to the 732 field position, and El Cid's STABLE for the Aquitanians duplicates the Umayyad cavalry theme
